spec_family.name: New Construction Interior Door Slab Stain/Clear Coat
spec_family.description: Covers stain application, sanding sealer, and clear topcoat for interior door slabs in new construction. Combined spec with coating_type dimension (stain_clear, stain_only, clear_only). Stain phase includes wipe step for all methods. Sealer and clear phases use independent application method selection. Uses EA as primary UOM (per door slab). Surface-specific dimensions include door_style and sides. Material systems are shared product-role-based recommendations. Context prefix DSST avoids collision with paint counterpart SF_DOOR_SLAB_INT_NC (prefix used in paint spec tasks).

includes: Stain application on bare wood door slabs (brush+wipe, spray+wipe)
Sanding sealer application (0-2 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Clear topcoat application (1-3 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Bare wood preparation (inspect, sand 120-150 grit, fill defects with wood filler, grain raise for waterborne, tack clean)
Wood conditioner application (softwood + stain, unless gel stain)
Interstage sanding between sealer coats (220-320 grit)
Interstage sanding between clear coats (320-400 grit)
Stain dry verification before sealer/clear application
Floor protection under door work area
Wall masking adjacent to door opening (spray or when walls are SS_PAINTED_*)
Door slab faces (both sides, independently assignable)
Door slab edges (hinge edge assigned to hinge side, latch edge to opening side)

excludes.item: Interior repaint stain (stripping existing finish, recoating)

excludes.route_to: Future exterior door NC stain spec

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary configuration dimension — drives layer stack, material systems, and module activation.
configuration_dimensions.notes: stain_clear is the professional standard for interior doors. stain_only is rare (unprotected stain). clear_only for natural wood look or pre-stained surfaces.

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, and coat count defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=budget (1 stain + 0 sealer + 1 clear = 2 coats). QT4=standard (1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 coats). QT5=premium (1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 coats).

configuration_dimensions.description: Stain application technique. All stain methods include a wipe step to control color depth.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for doors — most control on panel and edge detail. Spray for production volume. All methods include wipe-back step. No roll option for doors — panel detail requires brush or spray.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat application technique. No roll option — causes air bubbles in clear coat.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for control on panel detail. Spray for production. Roll PROHIBITED for clear coat.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat sheen. Drives product selection.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin is most popular for residential doors. No sheen/QT gate — all sheens at all tiers.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of stain coats. User-selectable with default of 1.
configuration_dimensions.notes: 1 coat is standard. 2 coats for deeper color saturation.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of sanding sealer coats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 skips sealer (budget). QT4 uses 1 coat. QT5 uses 2 coats.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of clear topcoats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 uses 1 coat. QT4 uses 2 coats. QT5 uses 3 coats.

configuration_dimensions.description: Door slab style. Controls production rate modifiers for stain and clear application.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Slab=flat flush door. Shaker=recessed panel. Raised panel=profiled faces. Glass frame=french-style (masking glass adds significant time). Stain on panel detail requires extra wipe attention.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of door sides to stain.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Standard is 2 sides (both faces). 1 side for closet doors or doors where backside is not visible.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood species grouping. Drives wood conditioner activation for softwood.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Softwood (pine, poplar, alder) requires pre-stain wood conditioner unless gel stain. Hardwood (oak, maple, cherry, walnut) does not need conditioner.

paintable_items.name: Door slab
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each door slab as one EA. Sides dimension controls whether 1 or 2 faces are stained. Edges included with face count.
paintable_items.notes: Primary paintable item. EA per door slab. Door style modifier applies to stain and clear tasks.

variants.notes: Standard stain+clear. 4 total coats. Professional residential standard.
Production spray variant. Full protection required.
Stain-only, no clear coat. Minimal workflow.
Clear-only on natural or pre-stained wood. 3 coats.
Premium all-spray. Maximum production speed at highest quality tier.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of door slabs to stain
Floor protection area under door work zone

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: application_method_stain = spray OR application_method_clear = spray, or walls are SS_PAINTED_*
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Wall masking LF adjacent to door opening

protection_zones_required.notes: Drop cloths under door work area. Stain drips are especially hard to clean. Full coverage under door swing area.
Wall masking adjacent to door opening for spray. Also required when walls are SS_PAINTED_*.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Door slab and frame often share stain/clear finish. May be stained in same session.
Door slab adjacent to wall at opening. Stain is harder to clean from painted walls.

valid_input_states.notes: Bare wood is the primary input state. clear_only also accepts SS_STAINED (pre-stained wood needing topcoat only).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: When walls are finished, wall masking required for ALL methods. Stain penetrates painted surfaces.
When walls are unfinished, spray method still requires masking.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Stain door slabs typically before wall finishing in NC sequence. Staining requires bare wood.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Setup > Prep (sand, fill, grain raise, condition) > Stain coat 1 (+wipe) > [Stain coat 2] > Stain dry > Sealer coat 1 > [Sealer interstage > Sealer coat 2] > Sealer sand > Clear coat 1 > [Clear interstage > Clear coat 2] > [Clear coat 3] > Final inspect > Cleanup
sequencing_notes.notes: Unlike paint specs, stain has no companion prime spec.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC interior door slab stain/clear coat (Tier 2 in interior stain spec rollout). Key features: coating_type dimension, door_style modifiers (slab=1.0, shaker=1.25, raised_panel=1.35, glass_frame=1.80), sides dimension (1 or 2), independent stain and clear application methods, user-selectable coat counts with QT-driven defaults, 14 SOP modules, context prefix DSST.
